claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances. trip_record.actual_distance_km is 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-05009) and trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 8.5 km (EV-TRIP-05009), so under POL-RD-22 the deviation distance is 10.0 minus 8.5 = 1.50 km, and the derived block records deviation_km 1.50 with within_tolerance false against POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05009) shows which route was taken and when - the vehicle left the recommended BKE at Woodlands Avenue 2 and ran Woodlands Road until rejoining at Petir Road - but under POL-RD-22 the trace is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the recorded distances control. The deviation therefore exceeds tolerance by 0.50 km.

The reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The only traffic artifact covering this trip window is EV-ADVIS-05009-01, and that artifact is MISSING: it has no payload and its admissibility carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact (POL-GEN-02). The record therefore contains no TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended BKE segment in the trip window, and POL-RD-23 requires exactly that - congestion, an incident or a closure shown by such data - before a reroute is justified. The driver's assertion in MSG-05009-003, 'BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?', and his counterparty statement 'Got accident, I saw the jam on the map' are assertions with no such data, and POL-RD-23 says a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. I am careful about what this absence proves: it is not a finding that the BKE was clear, it is the absence of the data the clause makes a condition of justification.

On POL-RD-24's matrix exactly one row applies, and it is row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - refund of the excess distance fare in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD. That figure is carried on EV-FARE-05009 as derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.08, with per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 under rate card RC-SG-RYDEX-2026Q3 and surge_multiplier 1.0, and the fare ledger shows the trip was charged 14.05 SGD with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so nothing has yet been returned. The rider should receive 1.08 SGD as a PARTIAL_REFUND - part of the trip's charge returned, on POL-GEN-03's definition. On the amount I am straight with the tribunal: the rider asked for 3.50 SGD, but POL-RD-24's remedy for a deviation is the excess distance fare, and I do not ask for more than the clause provides.

The driver's notification and the rider's 'ok can' answer do not defeat the refund. The driver did message before the deviation - MSG-05009-003 at 15:49:39, ahead of the route_deviation_detected event at 15:51:59 - and the rider replied MSG-05009-004 'ok can' at 15:49:59 (EV-CHAT-05009), so the notification limb of POL-RD-21 is met and the chat record confirms the rider's acknowledgment. But that acknowledgment is decisive only where the reroute is also traffic-justified: agreement is an element of row (a) of POL-RD-24 and non-notification is the element of row (b), whereas row (d), which governs a reroute that is not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km, turns on traffic justification alone and contains no notification or agreement condition. The rider's 'ok can' was given on the driver's unverified accident report and cannot supply the traffic data POL-RD-23 requires.

This case is one for a ruling under row (d), not for escalation, and no open question stands in the way. POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling is not touched - the deviation is 1.50 km and over_ai_limit is false on EV-TRIP-05009 - and the dispute value is 3.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, in which the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (fraud_flags 0 on EV-RPROF-05009 and on EV-DPROF-05009), so no 0.95 threshold is engaged, and no safety flag is present. POL-GEN-26 has nothing to operate on here, because the fact the matrix needs - whether the reroute was traffic-justified - is answered by POL-RD-23 itself: a driver's assertion with no traffic data does not justify the reroute. The clause says so, so no outcome is being inferred from silence.

claims.text: The traffic question this reroute turns on cannot be answered from this record, and POL-GEN-26 names it. The only artifact that could carry that fact — EV-ADVIS-05009-01, the LTA traffic advisory for the recommended BKE segment over the trip window — is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) with weight_multiplier 0.0; under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact. POL-GEN-26 lists 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts that must send a case to a human reviewer when the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired, and the pre-pass records that this loss is the platform's own ('the platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed ... failed (feed timeout) and was not retried') and that the record is 'silent on traffic on the recommended route; this is not a finding of no traffic'. The advisory's derived tag justifies_reroute: false is that same absence restated — POL-RD-23 'has no traffic data to read' — and cannot be read as an affirmative finding that the BKE was clear; the rider's stated ground, that he 'could not find any accident news after', is his own post-hoc search and is not a fact in the record either. POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence on this fact at the absent artifact's 0.0, so no AI ruling can rest on it: the case escalates under POL-GEN-26, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and holds the fare rather than refunding it, because the open question is resolved against neither party.

The driver did what POL-RD-21 requires, and on that clause's own words this is an agreed deviation. He messaged the rider in-app at 15:49:39 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — and the platform logged the route deviation only at 15:51:59, so the notice preceded the point of deviation and carried a reason, which POL-RD-21 says is enough ('a brief reason is enough'); the rider read it and acknowledged at 15:49:59 with 'ok can', and his own claim text confirms it ('I said ok because I believed him'). The chat log is complete and clean (weight 1.0, no issues), and POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. This is therefore not a driver who took a passenger the long way unannounced; notice was given before the deviation, was read, and was agreed, and the only thing left open is the traffic datum the platform's failed feed could not supply.

Even at its highest, the rider's claim cannot reach the 3.50 SGD he asks back. The deviation is the platform's recorded 10.0 km actual less the 8.5 km recommended route = 1.50 km under POL-RD-22, i.e. 0.50 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance, and the fare consequence of that excess distance at the base rate of 0.72 SGD/km is 1.08 SGD — the figure the fare ledger's money block derives under POL-RD-24 and the figure POL-RD-24 fixes for the excess distance fare, rounded to the cent and without surge. POL-GEN-03 reserves FULL_REFUND for a filing party who is 'entirely right' and would return 'the whole contested amount'; the ledger shows 14.05 SGD charged, of which the time_fare (3.15) and the platform_fee (0.90) are untouched by the route, and nothing in the fare evidence supports 3.50 SGD. The rider's demand is therefore overstated as a matter of arithmetic, and any excess-distance award is capped at 1.08 SGD.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver. Nothing is paid and nothing is refunded today: this case goes to a human reviewer, and the 14.05 SGD fare (EV-FARE-05009) is held rather than collected or returned. Here is why, in plain language.

What the record does settle. The 23 Aug 2026 trip ran Causeway Point to Hillion Mall. The platform's own recorded distances on EV-TRIP-05009 are 10.0 km actual against 8.5 km recommended, so under POL-RD-22 the deviation is 1.50 km - over the 1.0 km tolerance and under POL-RD-25's 2 km ceiling for an AI ruling. The driver did notify the rider in-app before the deviation: MSG-05009-003 at 15:49:39 ('BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?') against the route_deviation_detected event at 15:51:59, and the rider read it and answered 'ok can' at 15:49:59 (EV-CHAT-05009). The notification limb of POL-RD-21 is met, and at the base rate on EV-FARE-05009 (0.72 SGD/km, POL-RD-24) the excess-distance figure would be 1.50 x 0.72 = 1.08 SGD. Those points are the rider's claim 1 and the driver's claims 2 and 3, and they are accepted so far as they go.

What the record does not settle, and why the AI cannot rule. POL-RD-24's matrix turns on whether the reroute was traffic-justified, and the only artifact that could carry that fact - the LTA traffic advisory for the recommended BKE segment over the trip window, EV-ADVIS-05009-01 - is MISSING: weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact. The pre-pass records that the platform's own request to the LTA feed timed out and was not retried, and that the record is 'silent on traffic on the recommended route; this is not a finding of no traffic.' POL-GEN-26 names 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts that send a case to a human reviewer when the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired, and the clause requires no outcome to be inferred from that absence.

So both of the two competing readings fail. The rider's claim that the case is a straight row (d) refund of 1.08 SGD is rejected: POL-RD-23 does provide that a driver's assertion of traffic with no supporting data does not justify the reroute, and the driver's bare assertion (in chat and in his statement, 'Got accident, I saw the jam on the map') therefore cannot win the traffic-justified limb - but it does not establish the opposite either, and with the carrying artifact absent the traffic limb is undecided, supporting neither a refund that needs justification to fail nor a no-refund that needs it to hold. The driver's claim that POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the missing artifact's 0.0 answers itself: a missing artifact carries no fact, so it fixes no cap; but nor does its absence prove the reroute unjustified. The driver's POL-RD-21 point (informed and agreed) is accepted as a fact, but it only decides between refund and no-refund once traffic justification is known - it is an element of rows (a) and (b) of POL-RD-24 and does not bear on row (d).

Open question for the reviewer: was the recommended BKE segment congested, incident-affected or closed between 15:46 and 16:04 on 23 Aug 2026? If it was, the driver informed the rider and the rider agreed, so no refund is due (row (a)). If it was not, the excess-distance fare of 1.08 SGD is refundable under row (d). The 14.05 SGD fare is held until that is answered. No referral issues: a route deviation has no referral clause in this policy version, and POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence bar for an AI ruling is not met on a pivotal fact this record cannot carry.

ruling.explanation: Rider and driver: the fare charged for this trip was 14.05 SGD. The platform's own trip record (EV-TRIP-05009) puts the recommended route at 8.5 km and the route actually driven at 10.0 km. Under POL-RD-22 (v2.1 1.3/1.4) the deviation is the difference between those recorded distances, 10.0 - 8.5 = 1.50 km. That is over the 1.0 km tolerance but under the 2.0 km ceiling in POL-RD-25 (v2.1 6.2), and the value is 3.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI may rule and the ruling is final at any confidence. The reroute was not traffic-justified. POL-RD-23 (v2.1 1.4) makes a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended BKE segment in the trip window the condition of justification, and says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The only traffic artifact here, EV-ADVIS-05009-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; under POL-GEN-02(3) a missing artifact carries no fact, and the record contains no traffic data at all. The driver asks me to escalate under POL-GEN-26 because traffic justification cannot be established. I do not, because POL-RD-23 settles that question on the record as it stands - no data means not justified - and POL-GEN-26 itself says no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence except where a rule says so; POL-RD-23 is that rule. The driver's account that he saw the jam on the map is an assertion without the data the clause requires, and the missing feed is named here so both sides can see what the finding rests on. The driver's notification point is accepted but does not change the result: the chat log (EV-CHAT-05009) shows he messaged at 15:49:39, before the platform logged the deviation at 15:51:59, with a reason, and the rider replied 'ok can' at 15:49:59, read at 15:50:31. Notice and agreement matter only to POL-RD-24's row (a), which also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified; the row that applies, row (d) (not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km), reads traffic justification alone, so the agreed notice does not defeat the refund. The applicable row is POL-RD-24 (v2.1 1.3) row (d): refund of the excess distance fare in full, which is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD (EV-FARE-05009, rate card RC-SG-RYDEX-2026Q3). The rider asked for 3.50 SGD, but the policy's remedy for a deviation is the excess distance fare, not the whole difference in what he paid - the time fare (3.15 SGD) and the platform fee (0.90 SGD) are not caused by the extra distance - so the demand is overstated as a matter of arithmetic. The rider is therefore owed 1.08 SGD, a partial refund of part of the trip's charge, and nothing is payable to the driver. No referral arises: this version provides no referral clause for a route deviation. No safety flag is set and neither profile carries a fraud flag. My confidence is 0.85: the deviation rests on the trip record at full weight (1.0), and the traffic limb is settled by POL-RD-23 on an artifact that carries no fact, so nothing below full weight carries the decision.

ruling.explanation:
To rider R-21688 and driver D-59126: the fare for trip TRP-05009 is adjusted. Of the 14.05 SGD charged, 1.08 SGD is returned to the rider; the balance stands.

THE DEVIATION. The platform's trip record (EV-TRIP-05009, weight 1.0) records 10.0 km actually driven against 8.5 km recommended. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is 10.0 - 8.5 = 1.50 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance (derived deviation_km 1.50, within_tolerance false). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05009, weight 1.0) shows which route was taken but, by POL-RD-22, is not used to re-measure distance. The deviation is inside POL-RD-25's 2.0 km AI ceiling (over_ai_limit false).

TRAFFIC JUSTIFICATION. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data - a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended BKE segment in the trip window - shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The only such artifact, EV-ADVIS-05009-01, is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0): the platform's request to the LTA feed failed and was not retried, so the record holds no traffic data. POL-RD-23 speaks to that state directly - a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The driver's message (MSG-05009-003) and his counterparty statement are assertions; they do not supply the data. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified.

THE DRIVER'S ESCALATION ARGUMENT. It is argued that POL-GEN-26 sends this to a human reviewer because whether traffic justified the reroute cannot be established, and that POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the missing artifact's 0.0. I do not accept it. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established, and it yields where a rule supplies the answer; POL-RD-23 is that rule, and the absence is not being read as 'no traffic' but as the failure of the condition POL-RD-23 makes a condition of justification. A MISSING artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)), so it is not an artifact that carries the deciding fact and does not cap confidence: the figures this ruling rests on - deviation 1.50 km, per-km rate 0.72 SGD, excess fare 1.08 SGD - are carried by EV-TRIP-05009 and EV-FARE-05009, both weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and the 0.80 bar POL-RD-25 sets is met. As POL-GEN-02(3) requires, the impairment is recorded: EV-ADVIS-05009-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. The record's silence is not a finding that the BKE was clear.

NOTIFICATION. The driver did inform the rider: MSG-05009-003 (15:49:39) preceded the deviation event (15:51:59), and the rider answered 'ok can' (15:49:59) - EV-CHAT-05009, weight 1.0 - which the rider confirms. That satisfies POL-RD-21, but it does not change the result: row (a)'s no-refund needs the reroute to be traffic-justified as well, and it is not.

THE AMOUNT. POL-RD-24 gives exactly one row - (d), not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km: refund of the excess distance fare in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the base per-km rate, without surge: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD (carried on EV-FARE-05009 as derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.08; rate card RC-SG-RYDEX-2026Q3, surge_multiplier 1.0). The trip was charged 14.05 SGD and nothing has yet been refunded (refund_issued_sgd 0.0). The rider asked for 3.50 SGD, but POL-RD-24's remedy for a deviation is the excess distance fare only, so 1.08 SGD is awarded and the rest of the claim is not made out. Under POL-GEN-03 this is a PARTIAL_REFUND - part of the trip's charge returned, read from the rider's filing - and no driver compensation arises. The value of 3.50 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flag and no safety flag applies, and the stated confidence of 0.85 is above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires.

One point for the file: the traffic question is answered against justification only because no traffic data was obtained. If the LTA feed is re-queried and shows congestion, an incident or a closure on the BKE at the trip time, POL-RD-24's matrix would move to row (a) or (b). That does not alter the outcome on this record.

To the rider and the driver: the route deviation is established, but the traffic question this case turns on cannot be answered on this record, so the fare is held and the case goes to a human reviewer.

The deviation. On the platform's own recorded distances (EV-TRIP-05009) the trip ran 10.0 km against a recommended 8.5 km, so under POL-RD-22 the deviation is 1.50 km — 0.50 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance, and well below POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling, so the AI could in principle rule on the deviation itself. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05009) shows which route was taken and when (BKE left at Woodlands Avenue 2, Woodlands Road, rejoin at Petir Road) but under POL-RD-22 it is not used to re-measure distance.

The obstacle. POL-RD-24's matrix turns on whether the reroute was traffic-justified. The only artifact that could carry that fact is the LTA traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05009-01, and it is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (the platform's feed request for this trip window timed out and was not retried). Under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and the record is silent on traffic: it is not a finding that the BKE was clear. POL-RD-23 requires positive traffic data to justify a reroute, and a driver's assertion alone does not justify it. POL-GEN-26 names 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts that must go to a human reviewer when the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired. The traffic limb is therefore undecided: it supports neither a refund that needs justification to fail nor the driver's position that needs it to hold.

The rider's points. The 1.50 km deviation is accepted. The arithmetic is accepted too — the excess distance fare would be 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD on EV-FARE-05009 (fare charged 14.05 SGD; refund issued so far 0.0). But the claim that the reroute is 'not traffic-justified' cannot be used: its only carrier is the missing advisory at weight 0.0, so a ruling resting on it would be capped at 0.0, far below the 0.80 confidence POL-RD-25 requires. The 3.50 SGD the rider asks back is above POL-RD-24's excess-distance remedy in any event.

The driver's points. The driver is right that the traffic question cannot be answered from this record. The driver is also right that he messaged the rider before the deviation (MSG-05009-003 at 15:49:39, ahead of the 15:51:59 deviation event) and the rider acknowledged (MSG-05009-004 at 15:49:59), so POL-RD-21's notification limb is met; but that matters only in the traffic-justified branch of POL-RD-24 (row (a)), which cannot be reached — row (d) contains no notification or agreement condition, and neither does escalation. The driver's account ('Got accident, I saw the jam on the map') carries no weight and does not supply the data POL-RD-23 requires. The 1.08 SGD ceiling the driver computes is correct arithmetic but is not reached either.

Outcome. Nothing is paid or refunded; the 14.05 SGD already charged stands and the disputed 3.50 SGD is held. The case is escalated under POL-GEN-26 so that a human reviewer can obtain the traffic record for the recommended BKE segment over the trip window on 2026-08-23 (15:46-16:04), after which POL-RD-24's matrix can be applied. A route deviation produces no referral clause in this version. Confidence is 0.0 — the weight of the only artifact that could carry the undecided traffic fact.

But that acknowledgment is decisive only where the reroute is also traffic-justified: agreement is an element of row (a) of POL-RD-24 and non-notification is the element of row (b), whereas row (d), which governs a reroute that is not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km, turns on traffic justification alone and contains no notification or agreement condition. ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances. trip_record.actual_distance_km is 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-05009) and trip_record.optimal_distance_km is 8.5 km (EV-TRIP-05009), so under POL-RD-22 the deviation distance is 10.0 minus 8.5 = 1.50 km, and the derived block records deviation_km 1.50 with within_tolerance false against POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05009) shows which route was taken and when - the vehicle left the recommended BKE at Woodlands Avenue 2 and ran Woodlands Road until rejoining at Petir Road - but under POL-RD-22 the trace is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the recorded distances control. The deviation therefore exceeds tolerance by 0.50 km.

The reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The only traffic artifact covering this trip window is EV-ADVIS-05009-01, and that artifact is MISSING: it has no payload and its admissibility carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact (POL-GEN-02). The record therefore contains no TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended BKE segment in the trip window, and POL-RD-23 requires exactly that - congestion, an incident or a closure shown by such data - before a reroute is justified. The driver's assertion in MSG-05009-003, 'BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?', and his counterparty statement 'Got accident, I saw the jam on the map' are assertions with no such data, and POL-RD-23 says a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. I am careful about what this absence proves: it is not a finding that the BKE was clear, it is the absence of the data the clause makes a condition of justification.

On POL-RD-24's matrix exactly one row applies, and it is row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km - refund of the excess distance fare in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD. That figure is carried on EV-FARE-05009 as derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd 1.08, with per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 under rate card RC-SG-RYDEX-2026Q3 and surge_multiplier 1.0, and the fare ledger shows the trip was charged 14.05 SGD with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so nothing has yet been returned. The rider should receive 1.08 SGD as a PARTIAL_REFUND - part of the trip's charge returned, on POL-GEN-03's definition. On the amount I am straight with the tribunal: the rider asked for 3.50 SGD, but POL-RD-24's remedy for a deviation is the excess distance fare, and I do not ask for more than the clause provides.

The driver's notification and the rider's 'ok can' answer do not defeat the refund. The driver did message before the deviation - MSG-05009-003 at 15:49:39, ahead of the route_deviation_detected event at 15:51:59 - and the rider replied MSG-05009-004 'ok can' at 15:49:59 (EV-CHAT-05009), so the notification limb of POL-RD-21 is met and the chat record confirms the rider's acknowledgment. But that acknowledgment is decisive only where the reroute is also traffic-justified: agreement is an element of row (a) of POL-RD-24 and non-notification is the element of row (b), whereas row (d), which governs a reroute that is not traffic-justified with a deviation over 1 km, turns on traffic justification alone and contains no notification or agreement condition. The rider's 'ok can' was given on the driver's unverified accident report and cannot supply the traffic data POL-RD-23 requires.

ledger.claim: The traffic question this reroute turns on cannot be answered from this record, and POL-GEN-26 names it. The only artifact that could carry that fact — EV-ADVIS-05009-01, the LTA traffic advisory for the recommended BKE segment over the trip window — is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) with weight_multiplier 0.0; under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact. POL-GEN-26 lists 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts that must send a case to a human reviewer when the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired, and the pre-pass records that this loss is the platform's own ('the platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed ... failed (feed timeout) and was not retried') and that the record is 'silent on traffic on the recommended route; this is not a finding of no traffic'. The advisory's derived tag justifies_reroute: false is that same absence restated — POL-RD-23 'has no traffic data to read' — and cannot be read as an affirmative finding that the BKE was clear; the rider's stated ground, that he 'could not find any accident news after', is his own post-hoc search and is not a fact in the record either. POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence on this fact at the absent artifact's 0.0, so no AI ruling can rest on it: the case escalates under POL-GEN-26, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalated case issues no monetary outcome and holds the fare rather than refunding it, because the open question is resolved against neither party.

The driver did what POL-RD-21 requires, and on that clause's own words this is an agreed deviation. He messaged the rider in-app at 15:49:39 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — and the platform logged the route deviation only at 15:51:59, so the notice preceded the point of deviation and carried a reason, which POL-RD-21 says is enough ('a brief reason is enough'); the rider read it and acknowledged at 15:49:59 with 'ok can', and his own claim text confirms it ('I said ok because I believed him'). The chat log is complete and clean (weight 1.0, no issues), and POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. This is therefore not a driver who took a passenger the long way unannounced; notice was given before the deviation, was read, and was agreed, and the only thing left open is the traffic datum the platform's failed feed could not supply.

Even at its highest, the rider's claim cannot reach the 3.50 SGD he asks back. The deviation is the platform's recorded 10.0 km actual less the 8.5 km recommended route = 1.50 km under POL-RD-22, i.e. 0.50 km beyond the 1.0 km tolerance, and the fare consequence of that excess distance at the base rate of 0.72 SGD/km is 1.08 SGD — the figure the fare ledger's money block derives under POL-RD-24 and the figure POL-RD-24 fixes for the excess distance fare, rounded to the cent and without surge. POL-GEN-03 reserves FULL_REFUND for a filing party who is 'entirely right' and would return 'the whole contested amount'; the ledger shows 14.05 SGD charged, of which the time_fare (3.15) and the platform_fee (0.90) are untouched by the route, and nothing in the fare evidence supports 3.50 SGD. The rider's demand is therefore overstated as a matter of arithmetic, and any excess-distance award is capped at 1.08 SGD.
